My thinking this year:

I have 6 mu total. Quzhou soil is alluvial loam, decent but the groundwater situation is getting worse — I keep my well irrigation to what the crop really needs. Fifty years on this land, I know what works.

Stevia is my money crop — the factory in Guantao buys dry leaf. I'll put 3 mu into stevia this spring, transplanted from seedlings around mid-April after soil warms. It's demanding on nitrogen during the rapid leaf growth in June–August, but too much nitrogen and the stevioside content drops — the buyer docks the price. So I hold N around 18 kg/mu, split: base fertilizer before transplanting, then two topdressings. I need 3 irrigations minimum here because leaf yield tracks water. Expect maybe 280 kg dry leaf per mu in a normal year.

The other 3 mu I run the traditional winter wheat → summer maize double crop. Wheat goes in early October, harvest early June; maize straight after, harvest end of September. I use Jimai 22 for wheat — it yields well here and handles our dry springs. For maize I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, proven in this county. Wheat needs 2 irrigations (wintering and jointing), maize needs 1–2 depending on rainfall. I plough before wheat every 2–3 years to break the compaction layer; otherwise rotary. I apply compound fertilizer as base and urea as topdress — my rates are a bit above what the extension recommends because I'd rather spend an extra 30 yuan than lose 50 kg of grain.

Pesticide: wheat gets 2 sprays (aphids + powdery mildew); maize 1 spray for borer; stevia usually 2 sprays — it gets some leaf spot in humid weeks.
